planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade; Shoshoni keeps the tiered, horizontal branching of full-size doublefile cultivars in a much smaller footprint.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade. Bred by the U.S. National Arboretum as a compact counterpart to the larger 'Shasta', Shoshoni reaches only about half the size of a typical doublefile viburnum while still producing the same dense, horizontally tiered branches lined in late spring with rows of flat, lacecap-like white flower clusters. Bloom is exceptionally heavy relative to the plant's size, followed by red fruit that ripens to black and draws songbirds in summer, and foliage that turns wine-red in fall. Its small mature size makes it a good fit for foundation plantings and smaller gardens where the species' typical 8- to 10-foot spread would be unworkable. Prune only lightly right after flowering, since heavy shearing removes the tiered branching structure that gives the plant its character.

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in late winter or early spring in moist, slightly acidic to neutral, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; this dwarf sport blooms on old wood, so avoid pruning until after flowers fade.

directions: Plant in moist, slightly acidic to neutral, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; 'Compactum' is a naturally dwarf sport of Korean spice viburnum, growing to roughly half the size of the species while retaining its full measure of fragrance. Dense, rounded clusters of pink buds open to white in early spring, releasing the same intensely spicy-sweet perfume that makes the species famous, but on a tidy 3- to 4-foot mound that fits foundation plantings and smaller gardens where the full-size species would quickly outgrow its space. Dull dark-green leaves turn wine-red in fall where summers stay cool. Like the species, it performs best in zones with reliable winter chill and can struggle to flower well in zone 8 and warmer. Site it near an entry or path so the fragrance can be enjoyed up close, and prune only lightly right after bloom.

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in late winter or early spring in moist, slightly acidic to neutral, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Aurora blooms on old wood, so avoid pruning until after flowers fade.

directions: Plant in moist, slightly acidic to neutral, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun. Aurora is prized for unusually dark red flower buds that open through shades of pink before fading to white, giving the dense, rounded flower clusters a two-tone glow in early spring that is showier than the species' typically all-white bloom. The spicy-sweet fragrance is just as strong as in the species, filling the garden on mild spring days. The rounded, symmetrical shrub reaches 4 to 5 feet tall and wide, with dull dark-green leaves that turn wine-red in fall, and small blue-black fruit that is often hidden by foliage but valued by birds. As with other Korean spice viburnums, reliable winter chill is needed for best bud set and bloom, so it performs best in zones 4 through 7. Prune lightly right after flowering only if shaping is needed.

common_name: Spice Baby Viburnum (Compact Proven Winners Koreanspice Viburnum)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in late winter or early spring in moist, slightly acidic to neutral, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Spice Baby blooms on old wood, so avoid pruning until after flowers fade.

directions: Plant in moist, slightly acidic to neutral, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. Introduced by Proven Winners ColorChoice, Spice Baby is a true dwarf selection of Korean spice viburnum, forming a dense, rounded mound only about 3 feet tall and wide — roughly a third the size of the species — while producing the same clusters of pink buds opening to intensely fragrant white flowers in early to mid spring. Its small, tidy habit fits foundation plantings, mixed borders, and large containers where a full-size Korean spice viburnum would be impractical, and it needs little to no pruning to hold its shape. Dark green summer foliage takes on burgundy tones in fall. Site it close to a patio, walkway, or entrance so its spicy-sweet perfume can be enjoyed at close range.

common_name: Compactum European Cranberrybush Viburnum (Dwarf Flowering and Fruiting Snowball Viburnum)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Compactum keeps the full flowering and fruiting display of the species on a much smaller shrub.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; unlike the related dwarf 'Nanum', which is grown mainly for foliage and rarely flowers, 'Compactum' is a dwarf selection of European cranberrybush that retains the species' full ornamental cycle at about half its typical size. Flat, lacecap-style clusters of white flowers open in late spring, followed by heavy sets of translucent red berries that ripen in fall and often persist into winter, providing food for birds and strong seasonal color. The maple-like, three-lobed leaves turn burgundy-red in autumn. Reaching only 4 to 5 feet tall and wide, it fits foundation plantings, mixed borders, and smaller landscapes better than the full-size species, which can reach 10 to 12 feet. It blooms on old wood, so prune immediately after flowering only if shaping is needed.
